title: BC Premier-elect condemns theft of $100k Jesus statue from Catholic school
description: SURREY, British Columbia ( LifeSiteNews ) — The Conservative premier-elect of British Columbia blasted the theft of a life-sized copper statue of Jesus from a Catholic high school, calling it a “disgraceful act” against people’s faith. On November 11, which was Remembrance Day in Canada, vandals sawed loose the life-sized copper statue of Christ at the newly opened Catholic St. John Paul II Academy in Surrey, British Columbia. The statue, located in the school courtyard, was placed on a stone table representing the Last Supper. … Arsons against religious institutions have skyrocketed in the last few years. Federal data show that there were 592 reported arsons from 2010 to 2022. However, approximately 423 of these acts of violence were from 2015 onward. Conservative MPs have urged Liberal MPs for some time to back a bill that, if passed, would make church arsonists pay for the damages they cause as “vandalizing places of worship is unacceptable.” The Liberals thus far have refused to back the bill and recently blocked a motion that called for a study on church arsons in Canada.
